quotes.text: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing towards your body) in front of your legs.
quotes.closest: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing towards your body) in front of your legs.

quotes.text: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart while holding a pair of dumbbells next to your hips.
quotes.closest: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart while holding a pair of dumbbells next to your hips.

quotes.text: Draw your shoulder blades down and back to push your chest out slightly and draw your belly button to your spine to engage your core.
quotes.closest: Draw your shoulder blades down and back to push your chest out slightly and draw your belly button to your spine to engage your core.

quotes.text: Bend your knees slightly hinge forward from your hips and allow the dumbbells to run along the length of your thighs and halfway down your shins.
quotes.closest: Bend your knees slightly hinge forward from your hips and allow the dumbbells to run along the length of your thighs and halfway down your shins.

quotes.text: Ensure that the dumbbells remain in contact with your legs.
quotes.closest: Ensure that the dumbbells remain in contact with your legs.

quotes.text: You should feel like you’re almost grazing your legs with your dumbbells.
quotes.closest: You should feel like you're almost grazing your legs with your dumbbells.

quotes.text: As the dumbbells reach halfway down your shins, push through your heels and use your glutes and hamstrings to bring your body upright, then extend your knees and hips to return to the starting position.
quotes.closest: As the dumbbells reach halfway down your shins, push through your heels and use your glutes and hamstrings to bring your body upright, then extend your knees and hips to return to the starting position.

quotes.text: Master a soft bend and your knees should stay behind your toes throughout each rep.
quotes.closest: Master a soft bend and your knees should stay behind your toes throughout each rep.

quotes.text: think about pushing your hips back towards the wall behind you, rather than down towards the floor as you would with a squat.
quotes.closest: think about pushing your hips back towards the wall behind you, rather than down towards the floor as you would with a squat.

quotes.text: You want to avoid looking straight ahead the whole time as your neck will become strained and arched when you get to the bottom of the movement.
quotes.closest: You want to avoid looking straight ahead the whole time as your neck will become strained and arched when you get to the bottom of the movement.

quotes.text: Rounding your back will allow you to reach closer to the floor, but also increases your risk of injury, and reduces the effectiveness of this exercise.
quotes.closest: Rounding your back will allow you to reach closer to the floor, but also increases your risk of injury, and reduces the effectiveness of this exercise.

quotes.text: Lean forward as far as possible without rounding your back.
quotes.closest: Lean forward as far as possible without rounding your back.

quotes.text: limit your range of motion to as low as your hip hinge allows. Hamstring flexibility is the deciding factor in how low you should go.
quotes.closest: limit your range of motion to as low as your hip hinge allows. Hamstring flexibility is the deciding factor in how low you should go.

quotes.text: your back should remain in a neutral position.

quotes.text: Inhale, brace your core slightly, and lean forward by hinging in your hips. Keep your knees almost completely extended.
quotes.closest: Inhale, brace your core slightly, and lean forward by hinging in your hips. Keep your knees almost completely extended.

quotes.text: Reverse the movement and return to the starting position. Exhale on the way up.

quotes.text: Note: you can stand on an elevation (for example a weight plate) if you want to extend the range of motion without hitting the floor.

quotes.text: You don’t have to touch the dumbbells to the floor, although it is OK if you do.

quotes.text: As you lower your dumbbells down past your thighs towards your shins, you should feel the tension in the backs of your thighs.
quotes.closest: As you lower your dumbbells down past your thighs towards your shins, you should feel the tension in the backs of your thighs.

quotes.text: If you’re not feeling it, focus on pushing your hips back, or check that you only have a slight bend in your knees.
